content.body:
The Sturmgeschütz III B was based on the Panzer III chassis and originally intended as a direct infantry support tank to blast enemy strong points allowing infantry advances to continue. For this purpose, it was exceptionally heavily armored in the front and, since enemy strong points don’t typically move much, it was seen as far more economical and efficient to place the gun in a hull mount rather than a complex and expensive turret system. Of course, despite constant reminders not to use it as a tank, it was constantly forced into that role by the demands and fluidity of the modern battlefield. It performed rather well, despite a fairly clunky aiming system more suited to long-range artillery than an antitank weapon. Its short-barrel 75 mm gun was adequate for close-in work but suffered at longer ranges as we saw with the Panzer IV D, which employed the exact same gun.
The drawbacks of the fixed-forward gun mount were mitigated by the design of a system allowing the gun to slew over a firing arc of roughly 22.5 degrees.
Nothing could make a short-barrelled gun more accurate, but some efforts were made to increase the anti-tank lethality through the introduction of the 75 mm HEAT round. Its lack of a machinegun of any sort made it particularly vulnerable to enemy infantry at close range, so having supporting infantry, such as it would employ in real life, is a very wise tactical approach to using this AFV in World War II Online combat.
The StuG III B is extremely well armored frontally but suffers from the lack of a turret meaning that you are unable to see around the tank with the gunner as you can in turreted tanks. This places a greater value on the commander; the moment he is dead, you lose all ability to view to the sides or rear of the tank. So you can’t risk him any more than necessary.
Good StuG players are tough opponents because they have learned the hard way how to be effective. Deploying the gun sight means opening up the top viewport (an easy shot for a good rifleman). The StuG III B can contribute extremely well as a mobile artillery piece for shelling targets from range and it is often employed in such a manner when assaulting enemy towns.
AP, HEAT, and HE rounds all have different ballistics, so you will need to practice to know roughly what performance to expect from various rounds (typically, HE/HEAT do not fly as far as AP). The range sights dial in for AP and this is the most plentiful type of ammo, so it’s not a bad idea to range a target with AP, and then increase your elevation slightly before firing HE.
Control Variations: Commander (crew 2) has a rangefinder (key R to operate) in binocular view. Crew 3 may not look through the gun sight until it is Deployed (D) which opens the viewport and places the firing sight in the view slit.
